findings.claim: Around one in five UK start-ups do not survive their first year.
findings.truth: The UK one-year survival rate for enterprises born in 2022 was 92.3%, so about 8% did not survive their first year.
findings.evidence: ONS Business Demography 2023, reported by GOV.WALES business demography 2023.

findings.claim: The Jan 2025 examiner report cited application to context as the single biggest discriminator between higher and lower-scoring answers.
findings.truth: The January 2025 examiner report identifies both knowledge of the specification content and application to context as fundamental reasons for differences in Section B performance.
findings.evidence: OCR R067 January 2025 examiner report, Section B overview.

findings.claim: There are two core purposes of market research for a start-up.
findings.truth: The specification lists six purposes: reduce risk, aid decision making, understand the market, gain customers’ views and understand needs/wants, inform product development, and understand how a good/service complements others. Either present the current two as examples among the purposes, or revise all linked summaries and recall prompts to cover the full list.

The specification lists five benefits. The lesson splits the single benefit of matching and meeting specific customer needs into two overlapping benefits. Either use a five-benefit list throughout, or retain both phrasings but make clear that they describe the same benefit.

findings.claim: The rent-rise mark scheme calls £2,500 revenue and does not give the original or new profit.
findings.truth: At 500 candles, revenue is £4,000, variable costs are £1,500, and profit falls from £750 to £400 when fixed costs rise from £1,750 to £2,100.
findings.evidence: Recomputation from the figures in practice question 5.

findings.claim: The extended-response evaluation question in the written exam always focuses on Topic Area 4 (marketing).
findings.truth: The specification says that the one extended-response question relates to Topic Area 4, which covers the marketing mix and other marketing decisions; it does not restrict it to the marketing mix or prescribe an evaluation command word.
findings.evidence: spec 5.1 and spec 4.2, Unit R067, Topic Area 4.

findings.claim: This lesson feeds directly into extended-response evaluation questions on the marketing mix, which account for a significant share of the written exam.
findings.truth: The specification provides one extended-response question relating to Topic Area 4 and does not allocate a significant share of the paper to marketing-mix extended responses.
findings.evidence: spec 5.1 and spec 4.2, Unit R067, Topic Area 4.

findings.claim: The extended-response evaluation question on the marketing mix rewards answers that show how pricing connects to the other three Ps.
findings.truth: The specification only fixes the extended response to Topic Area 4; it does not state that it will be a marketing-mix evaluation question. Pricing is one of the marketing-mix elements when that is the focus of a question.
findings.evidence: spec 5.1 and spec 4.2, Unit R067, Topic Areas 4.1 and 4.10.

findings.claim: The lesson says there are eight sources of support, then names banks and business angels separately alongside seven other sources.
findings.truth: The specification has eight categories: finance providers (including banks and business angels), local council enterprise department, accountants, solicitors, friends/family, Chamber of Commerce, government, and charities.

summary: Seven verified findings have surgical edits. Two linked curriculum-list issues are recorded for adjudication because correcting them consistently would require wider changes across their lesson fields.
